species.name: Institutional letterhead / self-introduction boilerplate
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the comment opens with formal organizational self-identification: a legal/organization name, a membership-size or scope statement ('a national trade association representing...', 'has more than X members'), and/or a docket-number 'Re:' line in standard business-letter format. A 10 is a comment that leads with this kind of institutional self-introduction before any substantive point. A 0 is a comment with no organizational identification at all -- purely a personal first-person voice with no letterhead, mission statement, or 'Re:' line.
species.rationale: R03 (Student Loan Servicing Alliance: 'is a non-profit trade association made up of approximately 25 major student loan servicers...') and R16 (Center for Biological Diversity: 'has more than 1.7 million members and online activists...') both open with this exact self-introduction pattern and sit in the dense_low_card_high half; the scorecard bank plausibly rewards this institutional framing even though it is a resourcing signal, not a substantive one.
species.upstream_parent: the submitting organization's professional resources and standing (trade association, agency, corporation) versus an unaffiliated individual

species.name: Templated / mass-mail campaign boilerplate
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on evidence that the comment is a mail-merge or advocacy-campaign artifact rather than independently drafted: embedded email routing headers ('From:/To:/Date:/Subject:'), a scan/export footer with a filename and timestamp, or paragraphs that read as a reusable template rather than personal composition. A 10 shows multiple such artifacts. A 0 shows a comment that reads as independently composed with no campaign or mail-merge trace.
species.rationale: R02 and R41 are two near-identical Environmental Defense Fund 'Rolling back Clean Car Standards is bad for America' emails submitted a day apart by different named individuals, both carrying the same From/To/Subject header block and a '.txt[date time]' export footer; the underlying argument is identical regardless of who signed, so the template itself is not additional evidence of merit.
species.upstream_parent: a coordinated advocacy campaign using an email/action-alert tool to generate near-identical submissions from many signers

species.name: Self-reported professional credential preface
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment opens by explicitly stating the writer's job title, years of experience, or professional degree before or instead of grounding the argument in specifics ('I have piloted aircraft for over 43 years...', 'I am an occupational therapist...', 'My name is X. I am an independent living specialist...'). A 10 is a clear, specific credential statement placed prominently. A 0 is a comment with no self-credentialing at all -- an anonymous or unaffiliated first-person opinion.
species.rationale: R11 opens 'I have piloted aircraft for over 43 years and have been on every side of the certification process...' and R60 opens 'My name is Sarah Bucic and I have been a RN for over 20 years... on behalf of the Alliance of Nurses for Healthy Environments' -- both lead with a credential announcement before the substantive point, which can travel with real expertise but is itself just a stated claim, not demonstrated content.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter's professional seniority or standing in the sector being regulated

species.name: Regulatory citation apparatus density
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on the density of formal citation scaffolding used to frame the document -- docket numbers, CFR/USC pincites, Federal Register page citations, footnoted statute/case cites -- independent of whether that apparatus is load-bearing for the argument. A 10 is a comment saturated with this kind of legal-brief citation formatting throughout. A 0 has no citations or docket-style formatting of any kind.
species.rationale: R16 stacks footnoted statutory and Federal Register cites ('16 U.S.C. Section 1539(j)(2)(A)', '87 Fed. Reg 34625') and R49 does the same with ASTM standard numbers, '40 CFR Section 312.11', and a Federal Register pincite -- this citation scaffolding is a formatting tell of professional drafting capacity that can co-occur with, but is separable from, actual argument quality.
species.upstream_parent: professional or legal drafting assistance (law firm, trade-association counsel, or regulatory-affairs staff) producing the submission

species.name: Restates the rule's own text as the comment's point
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much of the comment's central content is a direct quote or close paraphrase of language from the proposed rule's own summary/background section, offered back as if it were the commenter's original observation, versus bringing in outside information the commenter evidently possesses independently. A 10 is a comment that is substantially a restatement of the rule's own framing followed by a brief reaction. A 0 brings clearly independent facts, data, or argument not traceable to the rule's own text.
species.rationale: R20 quotes the rule's own background clause verbatim ('(3) written company policies against sales to minors and other restrictions...') and then reacts to it as if it were new information, and R08 restates the FAA's own satellite-navigation/safety rationale nearly point-for-point before agreeing with it -- in neither case does the restatement itself demonstrate the commenter's own independent judgment.
species.upstream_parent: the comment was produced as a classroom or civic-engagement exercise rather than by a genuinely interested stakeholder
all_names: Restates the rule's own text as the comment's point

species.name: Scanned/faxed physical-document artifacts (OCR noise, stamps)
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on visible marks that the text originated from a scanned, faxed, or mailed physical document rather than a native digital web-form entry: garbled OCR character strings, broken word-spacing from multi-column layout, date-stamped footers, or 'RECEIVED'/'POSTMARKED' stamps. A 10 shows clear, heavy artifacts of this kind. A 0 is clean native digital text with no scan or transmission artifacts.
species.rationale: R15 carries visible 'RECEIVED OCT 0 91018' and 'POSTMARKED OCT 0 2 2018' stamps plus a garbled signature-block OCR artifact ('a-ge (cid:9)'), and R52 is a 1994 fax whose OCR output is heavily corrupted (stray symbols like '1'Cii9', '\1\', a telex number) -- the submission's physical-origin channel is unrelated to the strength of its argument.
species.upstream_parent: the submission channel/era -- a mailed or faxed physical letter processed into the docket rather than typed directly into an electronic comment form
all_names: Scanner and fax residue from a paper-route submission

species.name: 'See attached' transmittal shell before letter body
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the visible comment text opens with a short transmittal phrase ('See attached file(s)', 'Please see attached') that functions as a cover note for an appended PDF letter, rather than the comment being composed directly for the field. A 10 is a comment that is essentially just this transmittal phrase followed by the full pasted letter body. A 0 is composed directly with no attachment-transmittal framing.
species.rationale: R07 ('See attached file(s)' followed by the New Mexico Department of Agriculture's full letter) and R17 ('Please see attached.' followed by American Airlines' full technical letter) both use this shell; the capacity to produce and attach a formatted PDF plausibly correlates with institutional resourcing, though the transmittal phrase itself carries no argument content.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter has in-house document-production capacity (letterhead templates, a PDF export/attachment workflow) typical of an organization rather than a lone individual typing into a web form
all_names: 'See attached' transmittal shell before letter body

species.name: Procedural meta-commentary instead of a substantive position
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much of the comment is about the rulemaking process itself -- requesting a comment-period extension, criticizing the agency's internal culture or workflow, describing notice-and-comment mechanics -- rather than taking a position on specific rule provisions. A 10 is a comment that is entirely or almost entirely procedural in this sense. A 0 engages exclusively with the substance of specific rule provisions with no procedural content.
species.rationale: R19 is entirely a request from North America's Building Trades Unions for a 60-day comment-period extension with no position on the miner-training rule's actual content, and R29 is framed as a critique of FEMA's internal 'denial-biased' organizational mindset and process design rather than a specific regulatory provision -- both channels can co-occur with well-resourced regulatory-affairs staff without themselves engaging the rule's substance.
species.upstream_parent: professional regulatory-affairs or lobbying practice that treats procedural maneuvering (extension requests, process critique) as a comment strategy in itself
all_names: Procedural meta-commentary instead of a substantive position

species.name: Local/property-specific personal stake disclosure
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment discloses a specific personal or property stake tied to a named location near the regulated site or facility -- a home address, a stated distance from a facility, or a family/property impact narrative. A 10 gives a specific address or named-landmark proximity plus a personal-impact statement. A 0 gives no locational or personal-stake information at all -- a purely general policy opinion.
species.rationale: R15 states 'My family and I own property at 805 Schaper Ave., Washington, MO 63090, two blocks south of the Sporlan Valve Plant #1 Superfund Site,' and R09 grounds its PFAS comment in the specific Blades, Delaware site and its private wells and farms -- disclosing a concrete local stake can travel with genuinely site-specific first-hand knowledge, but the disclosure itself is a locational fact, not an argument.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter's direct personal or property relationship to a specific regulated site

species.name: Explicit non-expert / no-standing hedging disclaimer
species.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment contains an explicit disclaimer of expertise, authority, or standing to comment ('we have no specific recommendations but...', 'I'm commenting purely out of interest', 'I speak on my own behalf and not on behalf of anyone affected') placed close to its substantive claims. A 10 has a clear, explicit hedge of this kind. A 0 asserts standing or expertise, or makes its claims with no self-doubt framing at all.
species.rationale: R10 states 'We have no specific recommendations but encourage the Secretary to take all reasonable measures...' and R59 states 'I speak on my behalf and not on behalf of anyone affected by NHTSA's. I'm commenting purely out of interest in this matter' -- both explicitly flag a lack of standing/expertise immediately around their substantive request, a stylistic hedge that is separable from whether the underlying point is sound.
species.upstream_parent: the submitter's self-assessed lack of specialized standing or expertise relative to the docket's technical subject matter

species.name: Administrative transmittal apparatus dominates the extracted text
species.instruction: Score how much of the visible text is correspondence machinery rather than argument. Machinery means: printed letterhead blocks (street address, suite, mail bin, phone, fax, website), routing lines such as VIA E-MAIL or Submitted electronically via regulations.gov, mail-stop and room numbers, a Re: docket caption, repeated page-header furniture on continuation pages (addressee / docket number / page N / date), a formal signature block with title, a cc: distribution list, and an enclosure count. 10 = roughly a third or more of the visible text is this machinery, with four or more distinct apparatus elements present. 5 = a docket caption and a formal signature block but little other furniture. 0 = plain typed prose with no address block, no caption line, no formal signature block, and no distribution list.
species.rationale: The apparatus is produced by a back office, not by the analyst who thought about the rule, so it indexes who typed and mailed the letter rather than what the letter argues. It is dense in R01 (airport authority letterhead, fax number, continuation-page headers), R08 (Southern Company mail-bin block and a full corporate boilerplate footnote before any argument), R45 (Ref /A/-/E/ index, cc list of four names, encl (5)) and R18 (governor and director name plates, building and PO box block). Because the machinery scales with staff support rather than with the substance of the point, a judge can score it while remaining blind to whether the point is good. Tagged mixed because well-staffed submitters plausibly also write better-evidenced comments.
species.upstream_parent: An organisation with dedicated administrative or legal support staff who format, caption and route outgoing correspondence
all_names: Administrative transmittal apparatus dominates the extracted text

species.name: Addressed to the right named official with exact internal routing codes
species.instruction: Score how precisely the comment is aimed at a specific human at the agency and at the agency's exact internal routing string. 10 = the salutation names an individual and their real current title, and the address block reproduces internal routing tokens exactly, for example a mail code, a room number, a bracketed proposal identifier of the form CC:PA:LPD:PR (REG-nnnnnn-nn), or a named division and its acting chief. 5 = names a senior official generically (Administrator, Secretary, Commissioner) with a correct docket number but no internal routing tokens. 0 = To Whom It May Concern, Dear Sir or Madam, Dear Friends, or no salutation at all.
species.rationale: Knowing the individual, the mail code and the room number is knowledge about the agency, acquired through repeated contact or purchased with counsel; it is orthogonal to whether the substantive point is right. Compare R25 (Dear Deputy Assistant Secretary McHugh, by name and exact title), R22 and R45 (exact IRS and FAA routing strings, named engineer) and R10 (named certification-office engineer at his branch address) against R02 and R59, which reach the same dockets with no addressee at all. Tagged mixed because the same drafters who know the routing are often the drafters with real technical depth.
species.upstream_parent: A prior working relationship with the agency, or a lobbyist / regulatory-counsel drafter who knows which desk the filing lands on
all_names: Addressed to the right named official with exact internal routing codes

species.name: Opening asserts constituency scale before making any argument
species.instruction: Score how strongly the comment opens by quantifying who the submitter speaks for. 10 = an early paragraph or first footnote states membership counts, customers served, market share, revenue, jobs, or number of affiliated organisations, and does so before any substantive point is reached. 5 = the submitter names its sector role or coalition identity without numbers. 0 = no description at all of the submitter's size, reach, or represented population.
species.rationale: The scale claim is a bid for standing, not an argument about the rule, and it is a direct textual readout of an unseen factor (how big and well resourced the submitter is). It is explicit in R13 (more than 1.7 million members and online activists), R08 (9 million customers, plus an unrelated awards paragraph), R25 (fourteen affiliated unions, three million construction workers) and R54 (member firms comprising 99 percent of world pectin production), and is entirely absent from R32, R37 and R40, which argue the merits from the first sentence. Tagged mixed because organisational scale plausibly also buys genuine evidence-gathering capacity.
species.upstream_parent: Organisational resources and sector standing, plus a communications habit of asserting representational weight to earn attention
all_names: Opening asserts constituency scale before making any argument

species.name: Defers to and endorses another party's separate filing
species.instruction: Score how much of the comment's substance is delegated to a different commenter's submission. 10 = the comment explicitly concurs with, supports, or incorporates by reference the comments filed by a named association, coalition partner, government, or other submitter, and leans on that filing to carry the technical case. 5 = mentions coalition alignment or co-signatories without pointing at anyone else's filing. 0 = makes its entire case on its own and references no other commenter.
species.rationale: Endorsement-by-reference reveals that the real analytic work happened elsewhere, inside a coalition the reader cannot see, and it changes the shape of the visible text (short, deferential, with a named third party) without changing what the submitter itself contributed. It is the whole content of R15 (the Government of Chile supports the technical concerns submitted by ASOEX), and is the pivot of R12 (GDOT supports the comments and recommendations submitted by AASHTO, then adopts AASHTO's mileage figure) and R01 (the Airport Authority generally concurs with the comments submitted by the American Association of Airport Executives). R13 shows the multi-organisation variant.
species.upstream_parent: Membership in a coordinated trade association or advocacy coalition whose staff carried the primary filing on this docket
all_names: Defers to and endorses another party's separate filing

species.name: Reads as a graded course assignment rather than a stakeholder filing
species.instruction: Score how much the comment resembles a student writing exercise. Marks of a 10: explicit assignment or student framing (Final Assignment, we are masters students at X); an opening that paraphrases the notice's own background section back to the agency before opining; a five-paragraph shape with a thesis and a restating close; hedged conviction verbs (I believe, I strongly believe) standing in for evidence; general-audience or commercial web pages cited as authority (law-firm blogs, marketing sites); statistics quoted that are adjacent to but not about the rule; and no operational detail the writer could only know from inside the sector. 5 = essayistic and general but with one concrete sector-specific fact. 0 = the writer supplies operational, regulatory or technical detail from direct working knowledge and never gestures at the act of commenting itself.
species.rationale: This is an upstream factor with a very specific fingerprint and no merit content: a course deadline, not an interest in the outcome, generated the text. R23 carries the literal header Final Assignment and cites a law-firm blog and a pedestrian-fatality statistic unrelated to inflators; R38 identifies its authors as masters students at a policy school; R29 and R43 open by restating what the notice is inviting and then argue entirely from I believe. R03 and R06 show the same shape without the self-identification.
species.upstream_parent: The comment was produced as a classroom assignment or course exercise rather than by a party with a stake in the rule
all_names: Reads as a graded course assignment rather than a stakeholder filing

species.name: Campaign mailer envelope wrapped around a templated body
species.instruction: Score the evidence that the text was generated and mailed by an organisation on a signer's behalf. 10 = an email envelope from an advocacy organisation's action address survives at the top (From / To / Date / Subject lines, the official addressed by surname), the body runs through interchangeable campaign paragraphs whose facts and phrasing would sit unchanged in any signer's copy, and the close is an auto-appended block of full postal address, phone and email, sometimes with an export filename and timestamp footer. 5 = clearly templated argument paragraphs but no envelope or export furniture. 0 = individually composed prose with no template scaffolding, no envelope, and no auto-appended contact block.
species.rationale: R05 and R16 are the same campaign: both carry the identical envelope (From: Environmental Defense Fund takeaction@edf.org, To: Pruitt, Scott), the same China / 70-percent-EV-increase paragraph, the same closing technical-review paragraph, and the same export footer pattern (10822.txt and 4255.txt with a 4/5/2018 timestamp). The signer-specific text is a thin top layer. Whatever a scorer perceives here is a property of the campaign's copywriter, so it cannot be evidence of this submitter's contribution.
species.upstream_parent: A coordinated mass-comment campaign that drafted the text and transmitted it under the signer's name
all_names: Campaign mailer envelope wrapped around a templated body

species.name: Unrepresented individual narrating personal standing and exposure
species.instruction: Score how much the comment establishes the writer as a private person speaking for themselves through lived exposure to the rule. 10 = the writer names themselves and gives an occupation, tenure, or street-level location, and ties the rule to their own household, property, patients, students, aircraft or vehicle. 5 = first-person opinion with a stated role but no concrete personal exposure. 0 = written throughout in an institutional plural voice on behalf of an entity, offering no individual experience.
species.rationale: Personal exposure is a fact about who the writer is, not about the quality of the regulatory analysis, and it produces an unmistakable register shift. R02 gives a street address two blocks from the Superfund plume, R17 opens with 43 years of piloting and examiner work, R30 reports receiving two personal denials and two appeals, R58 identifies as an occupational therapist in home healthcare, and R59 as a nurse of twenty years naming her own county. None of these facts bear on whether the proposed change is correct, but they are exactly what an unmediated submission looks like.
species.upstream_parent: No professional intermediary: the submitter is a private person writing directly, without counsel, association staff, or an editor between them and the docket
all_names: Unrepresented individual narrating personal standing and exposure

species.name: Repeat player manages its own record across the docket
species.instruction: Score the signs that the submitter is an ongoing participant curating its own file with this agency. 10 = the comment cites its own earlier submission to the same docket by document number or URL, or cites its own published plans and reports as authority, or references private correspondence with the agency or a manufacturer by ticket or message number, or certifies that it discharged a statutory procedural duty, or asks the agency to withdraw and replace a comment it filed previously. 5 = exactly one such self-reference. 0 = no reference of any kind to prior interaction between this submitter and this docket or agency.
species.rationale: Record management is a fingerprint of continuity of relationship, which is an unseen factor, and it leaves distinctive text that has nothing to do with the strength of the argument. R41 cites its own September 2016 comment by regulations.gov document number, cites two of its own state plans by URL, and certifies compliance with 49 U.S.C. 70103(c)(4)(A). R52 asks in a footnote that its own 22 March 2022 comment be deleted from the record and replaced. R45 cites its own Tech Request 81581899 and the manufacturer's reply message 81581899/005. Tagged mixed because sustained docket engagement plausibly also produces better-informed comments.
species.upstream_parent: A repeat institutional participant with a standing relationship to the agency and staff who track the docket over months or years
all_names: Repeat player manages its own record across the docket

species.name: Adversarial venting: epithets, sarcasm, moral accusation
species.instruction: Score the hostility and affective heat of the register, independent of whether the underlying point happens to be sound. 10 = mocking nicknames or name-calling aimed at officials, sarcasm aimed at the agency or at other commenters, accusations of bad faith or corruption as the explanatory frame, all-caps emphasis carrying anger rather than emphasis of a defined term, or a taunting close. 5 = pointed frustration or accusation of institutional failure expressed without insult or sarcasm. 0 = a level, courteous register maintained throughout, even where the comment disagrees sharply with the proposal.
species.rationale: Heat is a property of who was allowed to press submit, not of the argument's content, and this slice contains a clean band of it: R26 (President Tiny Hands and his kleptocrats, GOP wingnuts), R24 (Oh, I forgot... I already know the answer, MONEY, plus shouted DIS-allowed and DESIGNED), R21 (telling another commenter not to behave like a terrorist), R33 (we aren't inclined to be pussyfooting around, don't expect to be greeted by smiling people) and R55. Several of these carry real substantive claims underneath, so the channel separates register from merit rather than tracking merit.
species.upstream_parent: Absence of any professional editing or institutional review before submission; a personal grievance route into the docket rather than an organisational drafting process
all_names: Adversarial venting: epithets, sarcasm, moral accusation

species.name: Coordinated Campaign Residue
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment contains recognizable repeated campaign language, mass-appeal slogans, campaign metadata, or standardized calls to action; score 0 when the prose is clearly bespoke and docket-specific.
species.rationale: R30 and R44 share nearly identical Clean Car Standards language, formatting, and campaign framing despite different apparent authors. The repeated rhetorical package signals mobilization and template exposure rather than independently developed substantive reasoning.
species.upstream_parent: coordinated advocacy campaign

species.name: Professional regulatory drafting
species.instruction: Score 10 when the text has polished counsel-style organization, precise docket and provision references, issue-by-issue proposed edits, and administrability framing; score 0 when it is informal, unsystematic, and nontechnical.
species.rationale: R02 and R27 are highly polished, provision-specific submissions from sophisticated organizations, yet both rank low for the dense model and high for the scorecard. Professional drafting may improve real quality, but its textual polish can operate as a spurious score cue.
species.upstream_parent: Law-firm or professional regulatory-affairs drafting resources

species.name: First-hand local exposure
species.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter describes personal residence, occupation, direct exposure, or concrete local consequences tied to the proposal; score 0 when the comment contains no personal or geographically specific stake.
species.rationale: R38 identifies the writer's property inside a contamination plume, and R56 describes private wells, farms, and livestock in a named affected area. These fingerprints may drive dense scores through vividness and specificity, although firsthand experience can also constitute genuine evidence.
species.upstream_parent: Submitter's direct personal exposure or local victim status

species.name: Unpolished grassroots voice
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment has conspicuous spelling, grammar, repetition, colloquial phrasing, or novice explanations combined with an earnest personal stance; score 0 when it is professionally edited and technically standardized.
species.rationale: R01 and R13 use repetitive, unschooled prose with broad assertions, yet receive high dense percentiles. The dense model may interpret idiosyncratic authenticity as importance even though informality itself is not substantive merit.
species.upstream_parent: Limited editorial support and grassroots rather than institutional participation

species.name: Government letter template
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment visibly follows an agency or state-government template with official titles, letterhead-style blocks, enclosures, formal routing, and bureaucratic boilerplate; score 0 when none of those institutional-document markers appear.
species.rationale: R12, R46, and R50 are official state or emergency-management submissions with formal routing and institutional boilerplate, but all rank relatively low for the dense model. Government-document form can be mistaken for importance independently of the comment's actual reasoning.
species.upstream_parent: Government-to-government commenting channel and bureaucratic submission procedures

species.name: OCR and Attachment Provenance
species.instruction: Score 10 when the text shows document-wrapper language, duplicated covers, slide or page extraction, OCR corruption, attachment references, or other filing artifacts; score 0 when it is clean native prose without such artifacts.
species.rationale: R20 reproduces extensive FDA guidance text with attachment and page artifacts, R53 contains slide-extraction remnants such as vertically separated words, and R59 shows severe OCR and scan noise. These cues reveal submission provenance and resources, not comment quality.
species.upstream_parent: professional document production and docket-ingestion pipeline

species.name: Decorative citation authority
species.instruction: Score 10 when citations, statistics, URLs, or named authorities are numerous or prestigious-looking but weakly integrated, tangential, or used mainly to signal authority; score 0 when there are no citations or every citation is tightly connected to a specific claim.
species.rationale: R03 cites media and legal sources in a highly emotional submission without tightly integrating them into a regulatory analysis, while R58 begins with an encyclopedia-like citation block before an incoherent request. Citation presence may attract dense-model salience without proving merit.
species.upstream_parent: Copying, search-assisted advocacy, or authority-signaling drafting practices

species.name: Notice-language echo
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment repeatedly copies the proposal's wording, headings, or embedded questions and supplies generic agreement or disagreement; score 0 when it uses independent framing and develops facts not already cued by the notice.
species.rationale: R15 echoes the notice's wording about written company policies and training, and R24 reproduces the agency's supplementary-information question before rejecting it. Mirroring the prompt can look relevant to a dense reader without adding independent analysis.
species.upstream_parent: Drafting directly from the agency notice, questionnaire, or a response template

species.name: Maximalist scope expansion
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses the proposal as a springboard for sweeping ideological claims, multiple unrelated harms, abolition demands, or broad unbounded remedies; score 0 when it stays narrowly tied to one operational change.
species.rationale: R18 demands preservation of an entire habitat from all disruptive activity, and R45 calls for abolishing the ESA while addressing incarceration and private breeding. Broad agenda expansion may produce rhetorical salience and high dense scores without increasing rule-specific merit.
species.upstream_parent: Ideological or movement-based advocacy agenda

species.name: Institutional status display
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment foregrounds titles, membership or customer counts, organizational reach, prestige, longevity, or representation of many entities; score 0 when it gives no status or scale information beyond the specific issue.
species.rationale: R10 emphasizes Southern Company's customers, subsidiaries, history, and corporate profile, while R52 foregrounds the Center's 1.7 million members and national advocacy reach. Such status signals may affect perceived importance and dense scoring, although institutional capacity can also support genuinely stronger evidence.
species.upstream_parent: Submitter's sectoral standing, agency relationships, and organizational resources

species.name: Personal Stake Narrative
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment gives a sustained first-person account of direct exposure, loss, ownership, work, or personal risk tied to the rule; score 0 when it contains no personal stake and remains purely general.
species.rationale: R10 describes the writer's own denials and participation in input sessions, while R25 identifies the writer's own vehicle and personal safety concern. Such proximity may attract model attention through vividness even when it does not establish the proposal's broader substantive merits.
species.upstream_parent: submitter's direct exposure or affectedness

species.name: Credentialed Insider Self-Positioning
species.instruction: Score 10 when the author prominently states a professional license, senior role, years of experience, or close occupational relationship to the regulated field; score 0 when no expertise or role is asserted.
species.rationale: R11 foregrounds 43 years across several aviation roles, and R29 foregrounds 20 years as a registered nurse. These credentials can be genuine evidence of relevant knowledge, but the textual status signal itself may be rewarded independently of the argument.
species.upstream_parent: submitter's sector standing or seniority

species.name: Regulatory Redline Fluency
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses exact section, page, line, docket, defined-term, or replacement-language mechanics to propose a textual regulatory edit; score 0 when it makes only a broad preference without pinpointed regulatory language.
species.rationale: R15 and R31 carefully work through statutory and standards terminology, while R43 cross-references multiple aviation directives, bulletins, and figure changes. This fluency may identify a professionally prepared submission even when it does not prove that the requested change is meritorious.
species.upstream_parent: lawyer or specialist compliance-drafting support

species.name: Pseudo-Quantified Authority
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accumulates precise statistics, dollar amounts, percentages, named reports, studies, media links, or numerical forecasts as rhetorical support; score 0 when it contains no quantified or attributed authority.
species.rationale: R25 combines injury counts, dates, vehicle years, and external quotations; R36 combines production forecasts, industry damages, tax contributions, jobs, and academic estimates. Numerical density can look evidentiary to a text model without ensuring that the figures are relevant, accurate, or dispositive.
species.upstream_parent: professional advocacy research and briefing support

species.name: Moral-Urgency Amplification
species.instruction: Score 10 when the prose uses sweeping catastrophe, absolute demands, condemnation, intergenerational stakes, or highly charged moral language; score 0 when the tone is neutral, bounded, and technically dispassionate.
species.rationale: R27 frames the issue around protection for the greater good and future generations, while R47 invokes mass extinction, climate change, and demands a stronger listing. Emotional urgency may make comments unusually salient without adding rule-specific evidence.
species.upstream_parent: activist mobilization and issue salience

species.name: Enumerated Implementation Blueprint
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies a numbered plan, multiple operational steps, process redesign, implementation mechanisms, or detailed alternative architecture; score 0 when it offers only a position or single requested change.
species.rationale: R02 proposes a multi-part pathogen-control framework, R10 presents a seven-step organizational redesign, and R38 describes a cross-program risk-assessment system. Structured solutionism may be an artifact of professional planning style rather than proof that the proposed design is sound.
species.upstream_parent: consultant, engineer, or managerial drafting culture

species.name: Institutional Prestige Wrapper
species.instruction: Score 10 when the submission prominently displays government or corporate letterhead, senior officials, organizational mission language, or a high-status signatory; score 0 when it is an unattributed or ordinary individual submission.
species.rationale: R05 is submitted by an ambassador, R35 by a state agriculture secretary's department, and R56 by a senior vice president of a major company. Institutional presentation may cue authority and resources while remaining separate from the correctness of the requested policy.
species.upstream_parent: organizational resources and institutional status

species.name: Coalition Cross-Reference Density
species.instruction: Score 10 when the comment repeatedly names partner organizations, prior submissions, stakeholder consultations, or adopts another group's recommendations; score 0 when the submission is wholly self-contained.
species.rationale: R05 explicitly supports comments from the Chilean Exporters Association, R24 endorses an airport-association submission, and R42 supports AASHTO while describing state stakeholder input. Coalition provenance can signal organized influence and information access, but coordination alone is not substantive merit.
species.upstream_parent: preexisting coalition relationships and coordinated drafting
